name: Mobilizon cadence - weekly heartbeat (proof of life and the runway)

parameters.jsCode:
// H1 Config - Run Once For All Items. Head of the weekly heartbeat (`n8n/heartbeat.json`).
//
// One item, carrying the series table, the heartbeat's own window, and the exact GraphQL document the next
// node will send - the same document cadence's `02` sends, from the same file (`lib/queries.mjs`), so the
// heartbeat and the cadence cannot disagree about what "the group's calendar" means.
//
// It carries **no credential and asks for none**. `READ_SERIES_HISTORY` is the public document (measured
// 2026-11-04: it answers unauthenticated, which is why `simulate.mjs` can plan from a laptop with no token),
// so the heartbeat is proof-of-life without being a second holder of the Mobilizon password. `checkHeartbeat()`
// enforces that: no credential block, no Authorization header, and no write or sign-in vocabulary anywhere in
// the document.
//
// GENERATED FROM integrations/mobilizon-cadence/nodes/40-heartbeat-config.js - edit that file and rebuild.

/**
 * The series table - the one place a maintainer edits to change what this integration does.
 *
 * This file is the source of truth for both hosts: `simulate.mjs` imports it, and `build-workflow.mjs`
 * inlines it into the n8n "01 Config" Code node. There is no copy of it inside n8n to keep in step.
 *
 * Every value here is either quoted from the organizer's own Mobilizon rows or chosen as an operating
 * limit and labelled as one. Nothing here states a cadence as a fact about the club (D92 keeps frequency
 * words off the site); these are the spacing rules the automation will *try* to hold, measured from the
 * rows in `fixtures/group-history-2026-11-04.json` (read from the live instance 2026-11-04):
 *
 *   MPLS Math Club - Bimonthly Social       2026-05-08, 05-22, 06-05, 11-07   14 days apart, Saturdays
 *   Parallel Learning for Mathematical Minds 2026-11-11                        Wednesdays, "twice a month"
 *
 * If the organizer's real rhythm is not 14 days, change `everyDays` here - that is the whole point of
 * keeping the rhythm as data rather than as a rule engine.
 */

const INSTANCE = {
  // Measured 2026-11-04 on Mobilizon 5.2.4: the GraphQL endpoint on this instance is `/api/v1`.
  // `/graphql` answers 404 `{"msg":"Resource not found"}`, which is what the public docs imply you should
  // use - so the path is recorded here rather than remembered.
  baseUrl: "https://mobilizon.labradorius.com",
  graphqlPath: "/api/v1",
  // The n8n nodes use the absolute URL literally. This is here so a reader, and the build's own assertion,
  // can see which host this integration is allowed to write to.
  expectedHost: "mobilizon.labradorius.com",
  // The workflow's own clock zone. The trigger says 09:00 and this is what that means; leaving it to the n8n
  // instance default is how a schedule quietly moves when the host is rebuilt.
  timezone: "America/Chicago",
};

/**
 * Where the Mobilizon account lives - **by name only**. These are the names of environment variables set on
 * the n8n host (see README, "Credentials"); the workflow reads them with `$env`, so no password exists in the
 * repo, in the workflow JSON, or in the config item that every node can see. The build refuses this field if
 * it is ever given a value instead of a NAME.
 *
 * Mobilizon 5.2.4 offers no long-lived API token, and this workflow signs in per run with this account. OAuth
 * does exist on the instance - but on the apex (`POST /apps`), not under `/api/v1`, and its grants need a
 * one-time human authorisation plus a rotating refresh token (measured and read in lib/queries.mjs; D185), so
 * it moves the secret rather than removing it. If the operator chooses a scoped service account, `03 Sign in`
 * is the only node that changes.
 */
const CREDENTIALS = {
  emailEnv: "MOBILIZON_EMAIL",
  passwordEnv: "MOBILIZON_PASSWORD",
};

const RUN = {
  /**
   * `true` computes everything and writes nothing: the decision arrives as `would_create` with the exact
   * payload it would have sent, printed in the report. Flip to `false` after watching one dry run you agree
   * with. This is the only kill switch, so it is deliberately the first line of the config.
   */
  dryRun: true,
  /** Never write a date further out than this. A series whose rule points past the horizon is skipped -
   *  the club stays able to plan by hand, and a runaway loop cannot fill next year. */
  horizonDays: 28,
  /** How far past the last existing row the rule may reason while catching up. Past this the run alerts
   *  instead of inventing a chain of dates nobody asked for. */
  maxCatchUpSteps: 6,
  /** The read window, in days. Back: enough history to see the rhythm and survive a long gap. Forward:
   *  enough to see every date the club has already scheduled by hand. */
  readBackDays: 400,
  readAheadDays: 120,
  readLimit: 100,
};

/**
 * Execution retention, in the runtime's own words (D201, 2026-11-05).
 *
 * Measured on the live instance by A/B on a throwaway workflow: the YunoHost package ships
 * `EXECUTIONS_DATA_SAVE_ON_SUCCESS=none` and `EXECUTIONS_DATA_SAVE_MANUAL_EXECUTIONS=false` in its rendered `.env`,
 * so a successful run - manual or scheduled - is never persisted. The symptom is not an error: the run returns
 * an execution id, and reading it answers `Execution '2' not found`. A dry run nobody can read is a dry run
 * nobody ran, so both artifacts declare their own retention, and the A/B proved the workflow's settings beat
 * the instance default.
 *
 * Per-workflow rather than instance-wide on purpose (operator ruling 2026-11-05, "1c"): instance-wide `all`
 * would also keep every other workflow's run data - one of which may hold a password - and a hand-edited `.env`
 * is re-rendered from the package template at the next `yunohost app upgrade` (D199).
 *
 * What this costs, named rather than argued: with success data stored, this workflow's own run records hold the
 * sign-in request body. Whether n8n 2.45.7 masks a `$env` password inside stored run data is **not measured**,
 * so pruning stays a host job (docs/security.md) and `verify-import.mjs` prints this as a NOTE, not a pass.
 */
const RETENTION = {
  saveDataErrorExecution: "all",
  saveDataSuccessExecution: "all",
  savePreExecutionData: false,
  saveManualExecutions: true,
};

/**
 * The alert channel - **one topic on the operator's own ntfy server** (D194, adopted 2026-11-04).
 *
 * Measured on 2026-11-04 from this workspace (Linux), so a future session does not re-guess it:
 *   - `ntfy.labradorius.com` resolves CNAME `labradorius.com` -> `75.73.33.126` - **public**, not LAN-only,
 *     unlike `mobilizon.labradorius.com` (192.168.1.120). So the alert reaches a phone off the LAN, and
 *     nothing can poll the Mobilizon host from away from home.
 *   - Anonymous publish and anonymous poll are both refused: `POST /<topic>` -> `{"code":40301,"http":403,
 *     "error":"forbidden"}` and `GET /<topic>/json?poll=1` -> the same. `GET /v1/version` -> `40101`. That is
 *     the YunoHost package's own posture, read from its `conf/server.yml`: `auth-default-access: "deny-all"`
 *     plus `enable-login: true`, and `ntfy access everyone "up*" wo` at install (so **a topic must not start
 *     with `up`** - the package grants anonymous write-only there for its iOS upstream flow).
 *   - So the channel needs a credential: an ntfy **access token** in an n8n environment variable, exactly like
 *     the Mobilizon password (`CREDENTIALS`). ntfy tokens are `tk_`-prefixed and - measured from the upstream
 *     docs - "grant users full access to the user account", i.e. they are **not topic-scoped**. Least privilege
 *     therefore comes from the *account*: a purpose-built non-admin user whose ACL entry is
 *     `read-write` on this one topic and nothing else. See docs/operator-guide.md for the commands.
 *   - E-mail is not the channel: `labradorius.com` has no apex TXT (no SPF) and no MX record (measured
 *     2026-11-04 by `dig`), and the n8n package's pre-wired SMTP points at the YunoHost mail server that those
 *     records say is not set up for sending. Discord is the fallback (the repo already has a Discord webhook
 *     gate); ntfy was chosen because it is one `POST`, self-hosted, needs no bot, and works on a phone with no
 *     account beyond the topic.
 *
 * The URL is the **root**, not a topic path: ntfy accepts the whole message as a JSON body only when the
 * request goes to the server root ("To publish as JSON, you must PUT/POST to the ntfy root URL, not to the
 * topic URL" - docs, read 2026-11-04). That keeps the httpRequest node in the same `specifyBody: "json"` shape
 * as every other HTTP node in this workflow, so there is no second body style to review.
 */
const ALERT = {
  provider: "ntfy",
  host: "ntfy.labradorius.com",
  rootUrl: "https://ntfy.labradorius.com/",
  /** Topic ids in ntfy are `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}`. `mathloco-` prefixes it so a topic on a shared home server
   *  still says which project it belongs to, and it deliberately does not start with `up` (see above). */
  topic: "mathloco-cadence",
  /** Name of the n8n environment variable holding the `tk_...` token - a NAME, never a value, under the same
   *  rule as `CREDENTIALS` (the build refuses a value, and the token never enters the workflow JSON). */
  tokenEnv: "NTFY_TOKEN",
  /** What tapping the notification opens. The public schedule page, because that is the thing an alert is
   *  about, and reading it is how you tell whether the alert is stale. */
  click: "https://minneapolismathbookclub.com/#when-we-meet",
  /** Priorities are measured from the upstream table: 5 max (long vibration, pop-over), 4 high, 3 default,
   *  2 low (no sound, drawer only), 1 min. Nothing here is a 5: these messages arrive at 09:00 and a calendar
   *  problem is not a three-in-the-morning emergency. A run with nothing to say sends nothing at all.
   *
   *  `heartbeat` is the weekly proof of life (D205): quiet on purpose, because it arrives whether or not
   *  anything happened, and a message that buzzes once a week is a message that gets read.
   *  `runway` is that same message when the calendar it reports is empty further out than
   *  `HEARTBEAT.runwayDays` - the site's own staleness gate (A8, D188) would go loud about that, so the
   *  heartbeat stops being noise and becomes the early half of it. */
  priority: { problem: 4, wrote: 4, dryRun: 2, heartbeat: 2, runway: 4 },
  /** Only `warning` is used, because that tag name is quoted from the upstream examples. Other emoji tags are
   *  plausible but unverified here, and an unknown tag name is a message that fails to publish. */
  tags: { problem: ["warning"] },
  /** The message text is capped here as well as in the reporters, so a 400 from ntfy is not how a person finds
   *  out something went wrong. (ntfy's own limit was not measured; 1000 chars is far under the 4096-byte
   *  figure in the message-format docs, which is the number to re-check if this ever truncates.) */
  maxMessageChars: 1000,
  /** A second channel for the error watcher only, and it is **off** (D206).
   *
   *  The vendor set names the recursion trap outright: if the error workflow's own channel is the channel the
   *  monitored workflow uses, then the outage that caused the failure also eats the alert about it, and n8n
   *  does not re-trigger on the error workflow's failure ("no infinite loop, but the failure goes nowhere").
   *  Its mitigations are "use a different channel" or "have a fallback".
   *
   *  Shipped null because a fallback needs a secret that does not exist yet: the club's Discord side is a bot
   *  token for the site Worker (`DISCORD_TOKEN`, wrangler.toml), not an incoming webhook URL, and inventing an
   *  environment variable name for a credential nobody has minted is how a workflow ships a node that can only
   *  fail. To turn it on: create a Discord webhook for a club channel, put its URL in an n8n environment
   *  variable by NAME, and set
   *
   *      fallback: { kind: "discord", urlEnv: "MATHLOCO_ALERT_WEBHOOK", maxMessageChars: 1800 }
   *
   *  `build-alerter.mjs` then emits `A4 Notify on the fallback`, wired to `A3`'s error output, and
   *  `checkAlerter()` polices the pair (`onError` without the wire, or the wire without `onError`, is the
   *  silent-failure shape this repo has already been bitten by twice). Until then the honest statement is in
   *  docs/security.md: one channel, and the weekly heartbeat is the backstop for "the channel is down". */
  fallback: null,
};

/**
 * The weekly heartbeat (operator ruling 2026-11-05, "weekly heartbeat can be built now"; D205).
 *
 * What it is for: every other message on this topic means "something happened". D194's silence rule makes
 * that deliberate, and it leaves one hole no per-node error output can close - a scheduler that is simply not
 * running sends nothing, and nothing looks identical to a quiet week. A8's runway gate (`check:ics`,
 * N = 21 days, D188) is the only detector today, and it is a *deploy-time* detector on the *site's* snapshot,
 * so the honest latency of "n8n is dead" is about three weeks. One message a week cuts that to seven days.
 *
 * It trades directly against D194, which is why it was a ruling and not a code change: one message that means
 * "still alive" is the price of being able to notice death.
 *
 * It is not only a ping. It reads the same public calendar cadence reads (no credential - the same read
 * `simulate.mjs` makes) and prints the next date each series holds and how far out it is, so the weekly note
 * answers "is the calendar actually full?" as well as "is n8n alive?". Past `runwayDays` it goes to priority 4
 * and names the fix, which makes it the early-warning half of A8's rule rather than a third opinion on it.
 */
const HEARTBEAT = {
  /** 0 = Sunday ... 1 = Monday, measured against this instance's own node source: Schedule Trigger v1 takes
   *  `triggerAtDay` (an array of these numbers), `triggerAtHour` and `triggerAtMinute` - there is no `triggerAt`
   *  string (D207). `build-heartbeat.mjs` asserts its own trigger block against these three names. */
  weekday: 1,
  hour: 9,
  minute: 0,
  everyWeeks: 1,
  /** How far ahead of the next row the calendar may sit empty before the weekly note goes loud.
   *  Deliberately the same number as A8's `RUNWAY_DAYS` (scripts/check-ics.mjs, D188): one threshold for
   *  "the club is about to have nothing to attend", raised by the runtime at 7 days and by the deploy gate
   *  at 21. If one moves, move both, and the comment in check-ics.mjs points back here. */
  runwayDays: 21,
  /** The public read the heartbeat makes. Forward only: it is asking "what is coming", not re-deriving the
   *  rhythm, and a short window keeps the response small enough to read in one execution. */
  readAheadDays: 60,
  readLimit: 100,
  /** Structural, not decorative: the heartbeat has no `Tell a person?` gate, because a heartbeat that can be
   *  skipped is the same silence it exists to detect. `checkHeartbeat()` fails the build if an IF node appears. */
  alwaysSend: true,
};

const SERIES = [
  {
    key: "mpls-social", // stable id; never reuse it for a different series
    // Quoted from the organizer's row, verbatim. This string is the dedupe key as well as the new row's
    // title, so an edit here must match the Mobilizon title or the series stops being recognised (the run
    // will alert rather than silently create a second series).
    // The word "Bimonthly" is the organizer's, not ours: D92 keeps frequency words off the *site*, and the
    // harvester already quotes this title rather than rewriting it.
    title: "MPLS Math Club - Bimonthly Social",
    aliases: ["MPLS Math Club Social", "Bimonthly Social"], // earlier titles, so a rename does not orphan the history
    groupActor: "minneapolis_math_book_group",

    everyDays: 14,      // the spacing in the rows above
    weekdaySnap: 6,     // 6 = Saturday: pull the date back onto the club's weekday if a row drifts
    timezone: "America/Chicago", // declared, never inferred (see lib/core.mjs, "The clock rule")
    skipDates: [],      // "sometimes we miss one", as data: ["2026-12-19"]

    maxFuturePerSeries: 2, // stop once this many future dates exist; the club plans ahead by hand past that
    minLeadDays: 2,        // write anyway, but say so, if the date starts sooner than this
    strictTimezone: false, // true = alert instead of writing when a row's declared zone is not the series'

    // What the new row looks like to members
    visibility: "PUBLIC",
    joinOptions: "FREE",
    draft: false,            // true = park it as a draft for a human to publish
    copyPicture: true,       // carry the club's event art by reference (`picture.mediaUuid`), verified 2026-11-04
    blockOnSameDayConflict: true, // another group event already on that date -> skip and say so
  },
  {
    key: "parallel-learning",
    title: "Parallel Learning for Mathematical Minds",
    aliases: [],
    groupActor: "minneapolis_math_book_group",
    // 14 days is the club's stated cadence, not a measured one: Mobilizon holds exactly ONE row for this
    // series (2026-11-11, saved in fixtures/group-history-2026-11-04.json), so there is no gap history here to
    // take a mode of. "twice a month on weekday evenings" is quoted from that row's own description, and 14 is
    // also the spacing the social series' four rows show (14, 14, then a 155-day summer gap). Revisit once a
    // few parallel sessions exist - the anchor is the newest row, so history in Mobilizon is what this tracks.
    everyDays: 14,
    // No snap: 14 days from a weekday lands on the same weekday, so there is nothing to correct - and if a
    // human moves one session to a Tuesday, the next should stay a Tuesday. This series' own description says
    // "weekday evenings", not a named day. mpls-social keeps its snap because the club has stated a Saturday
    // pattern that a one-off weekday should not silently replace.
    weekdaySnap: null,
    timezone: "America/Chicago",
    skipDates: [],
    maxFuturePerSeries: 2,
    minLeadDays: 2,
    strictTimezone: false,
    visibility: "PUBLIC",
    joinOptions: "FREE",
    draft: false,
    copyPicture: true,
    blockOnSameDayConflict: true,
  },
];
/**
 * The GraphQL documents this integration sends, in one place.
 *
 * Both hosts run these same strings: the repo-side simulator (`../simulate.mjs`) and the n8n Code nodes
 * (the build inlines this file into them - see ../build-workflow.mjs). A query that is valid in one host
 * and stale in the other is the failure mode this file exists to prevent.
 *
 * Mobilizon 5.2.4, verified against `mobilizon.labradorius.com` on 2026-11-04 (see
 * ../records/2026-11-04-mobilizon-api-probe.md and ../records/evidence-2026-11-04.json):
 *   - the endpoint is `<base>/api/v1`, not `<base>/graphql` (the latter answers 404 `{"msg":"Resource not found"}`);
 *   - `createEvent` takes flat arguments, not an input object;
 *   - a GraphQL-level error comes back as **HTTP 200** with an `errors` array, so every caller must
 *     check for `errors` instead of trusting the status code;
 *   - the credential document is `login(email, password) -> { accessToken refreshToken user }`. There is no
 *     `sessionToken` field on this version, and HTTP Basic is not honoured at this endpoint (a bogus
 *     `Authorization: Basic` answers the same `unauthenticated` error as no header at all);
 *   - OAuth exists on this instance, but **not under `/api/v1`**: `POST /apps`, `POST /oauth/token` and
 *     `POST /login/device/code` are on the apex (measured 2026-11-04: `POST /apps` with an incomplete body
 *     answers 400 `invalid_request` "All of name, scope and redirect_uri parameters are required to create an
 *     application", and `/api/v1/apps` falls through to the GraphQL router - which is why the first probe in
 *     D177 concluded there was no client-registration route). The cadence still signs in per run: the grants
 *     this instance implements are `authorization_code`, `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code` and
 *     `refresh_token` - read in the upstream clone at f2590486f - so an OAuth token needs a one-time human
 *     authorisation and a rotating refresh token, which is a different secret to store, not no secret (D185).
 */

/**
 * One round trip per series: which group the events belong to (its actor id is `attributedToId`) and every
 * event in the window - past (the rhythm, and the row we copy) and future (the dedupe table, and the
 * "already scheduled far enough" check).
 *
 * `afterDatetime`/`beforeDatetime` bound the read so it cannot grow without limit as the club ages.
 *
 * This document is **public**: it carries no `loggedPerson`, so it answers with no errors over an
 * unauthenticated connection (measured 2026-11-04). That is deliberate - it is the read `simulate.mjs`
 * runs with zero credentials, and it means the n8n history node needs no secret attached to it. The ids a
 * write needs come from `READ_ACTOR_IDS`, which does.
 */
const READ_SERIES_HISTORY = /* GraphQL */ `
query CadenceRead($preferredUsername: String!, $after: DateTime, $before: DateTime, $limit: Int) {
  group(preferredUsername: $preferredUsername) {
    id
    preferredUsername
    domain
    name
    organizedEvents(limit: $limit, order: BEGINS_ON, orderDirection: ASC, afterDatetime: $after, beforeDatetime: $before) {
      total
      elements {
        id
        uuid
        url
        title
        description
        beginsOn
        endsOn
        draft
        status
        visibility
        language
        category
        joinOptions
        options {
          timezone
          isOnline
          showStartTime
          showEndTime
          maximumAttendeeCapacity
          hideNumberOfParticipants
          hideOrganizerWhenGroupEvent
          commentModeration
        }
        physicalAddress {
          street
          locality
          region
          postalCode
          country
          geom
          type
          description
        }
        picture {
          uuid
          url
          name
        }
        tags { title }
        metadata { key title value type }
        contacts { id }
      }
    }
  }
}`;

/**
 * The only credentialed request in the workflow, and the only place a password is ever sent.
 *
 * What comes back is a **session** token scoped to this execution, not a long-lived API key. Mobilizon does
 * offer OAuth apps on the apex (see the header: D185), but taking that route means registering a client, doing
 * a one-time browser or device-flow authorisation, and then carrying a rotating refresh token - a second
 * secret with its own failure modes, for a job that signs in once per run anyway. Two consequences of the
 * per-run sign-in worth knowing:
 *   - the refresh token is deliberately **not** selected. Keeping it would put a long-lived secret in the
 *     execution data for no benefit, since the next run signs in again in one round trip;
 *   - `user.actors` is selected because the write needs Mobilizon's internal actor ids, and hard-coding them
 *     survives exactly one account rebuild - and the failure it survives is the bad one (events attributed
 *     to the wrong actor, which look fine on the calendar).
 *
 * Verified 2026-11-04: the document validates against this instance (bogus credentials return
 * "Impossible to authenticate", not a validation error).
 */
const LOGIN = /* GraphQL */ `
mutation CadenceSignIn($email: String!, $password: String!) {
  login(email: $email, password: $password) {
    accessToken
    user {
      id
      actors {
        id
        preferredUsername
        domain
      }
    }
  }
}`;

/**
 * The write. Field-by-field variables (never string interpolation) so nothing the calendar holds can
 * become query syntax. `organizerActorId` and `attributedToId` are Mobilizon's *internal* actor ids, which
 * is why the read resolves them instead of the config hard-coding them.
 *
 * Selection set: the fields the audit step needs to prove the write landed.
 */
const CREATE_EVENT = /* GraphQL */ `
mutation CadenceCreate(
  $title: String!
  $description: String!
  $beginsOn: DateTime!
  $endsOn: DateTime
  $category: EventCategory
  $language: String
  $draft: Boolean
  $visibility: EventVisibility
  $status: EventStatus
  $joinOptions: EventJoinOptions
  $tags: [String]
  $metadata: [EventMetadataInput]
  $contacts: [Contact]
  $options: EventOptionsInput
  $physicalAddress: AddressInput
  $picture: MediaInput
  $attributedToId: ID
  $organizerActorId: ID!
) {
  createEvent(
    title: $title
    description: $description
    beginsOn: $beginsOn
    endsOn: $endsOn
    category: $category
    language: $language
    draft: $draft
    visibility: $visibility
    status: $status
    joinOptions: $joinOptions
    tags: $tags
    metadata: $metadata
    contacts: $contacts
    options: $options
    physicalAddress: $physicalAddress
    picture: $picture
    attributedToId: $attributedToId
    organizerActorId: $organizerActorId
  ) {
    id
    uuid
    url
    title
    beginsOn
    endsOn
    status
    draft
    visibility
    options { timezone }
    physicalAddress { street locality region postalCode country geom }
    picture { uuid url }
  }
}`;

/**
 * After the write: every row on the candidate date, in the group. Two assertions ride on this one read -
 * the event we just made is there, and it is the only row for that series on that date. That is the
 * duplicate guard that matters: Mobilizon has no conditional create and no idempotency key, so the
 * dedupe is "read, decide, write, then prove what the date now holds".
 */
const AUDIT_DATE_WINDOW = /* GraphQL */ `
query CadenceAudit($preferredUsername: String!, $after: DateTime!, $before: DateTime!) {
  group(preferredUsername: $preferredUsername) {
    organizedEvents(limit: 50, order: BEGINS_ON, orderDirection: ASC, afterDatetime: $after, beforeDatetime: $before) {
      total
      elements {
        id
        uuid
        url
        title
        beginsOn
        endsOn
        status
        draft
        options { timezone }
      }
    }
  }
}`;
const groups = [...new Set(SERIES.map((s) => s.groupActor))];
if (groups.length !== 1) {
  // Same refusal as cadence's 01 Config: this workflow reads one group per run. Saying so beats planning one
  // group and reporting the other as empty, which would look like a missing meeting.
  throw new Error(
    `H1 Config: series live in ${groups.length} different groups (${groups.join(", ")}). ` +
    "The heartbeat reads one group per run; add a second copy of the chain before adding a series elsewhere.",
  );
}

const now = new Date();
const stampDaysFrom = (n) =>
  new Date(now.getTime() + n * 86_400_000).toISOString().replace(/\.\d{3}Z$/, "Z");

return [{
  json: {
    runAt: now.toISOString(),
    groupActor: groups[0],
    SERIES, HEARTBEAT, ALERT,
    query: {
      // Forward-only window: the question is "what is coming", not "what was". The lower bound is today, so a
      // long club history never makes the weekly note's response grow without limit.
      readSeriesHistory: READ_SERIES_HISTORY,
      readSeriesHistoryVars: {
        preferredUsername: groups[0],
        after: stampDaysFrom(0),
        before: stampDaysFrom(HEARTBEAT.readAheadDays),
        limit: HEARTBEAT.readLimit,
      },
    },
  },
}];
